proposals.note: With pulse shape/rolloff fixed, occupied modulation bandwidth scales with symbol rate; other signaling families need extra assumptions.

original.question: Why do band-limited channels cause ISI?

proposals.reason: Loại bớt thành phần phổ có thể kéo dài xung và gây chồng symbol. Bộ lọc Nyquist đúng vẫn có thể không ISI tại thời điểm quyết định.
proposals.tip: Band limitation can cause pulse spreading; ISI is not inevitable.
proposals.note: Uncompensated bandwidth limitation can spread symbol pulses; a bandlimited Nyquist pulse need not cause ISI at sampling instants.

original.question: If average code length < entropy, result is:

proposals.reason: Entropy là cận dưới độ dài trung bình cho mã nguồn không mất mát theo các giả thiết thông thường.
proposals.note: A uniquely-decodable binary lossless code obeys expected length >= entropy in bits under the standard symbol/block model.

original.question: Given Eb/N0 increases by 3 dB, BER will:

proposals.note: For coherent BPSK in AWGN, Pb=Q(sqrt(2Eb/N0)); its high-SNR tail decreases approximately exponentially, not universally for every channel.

original.question: Why does DPSK eliminate the need for PLL?

changes.question: Why can noncoherent differential DPSK detection avoid an absolute carrier-phase reference?

proposals.reason: So sánh pha với symbol trước thay vì một pha tuyệt đối; vẫn cần đồng bộ thời gian/tần số phù hợp.
proposals.tip: DPSK differential detector → previous symbol as phase reference.
proposals.note: Differential phase detection uses the previous symbol as a reference, avoiding an absolute carrier-phase reference; timing/frequency synchronization are still needed.

original.question: If roll-off between subcarriers is incorrect, OFDM will:

original.question: What happens if carrier phase is not synchronized in coherent detection?

proposals.note: A carrier-phase mismatch rotates/mixes I and Q components for a general nontrivial phase offset; exact multiples of pi cause special sign cases.

original.question: In BPSK constellation, decision threshold is:

original.question: Why is Huffman coding optimal?

proposals.tip: Huffman optimal → symbol-by-symbol binary prefix code.
proposals.note: Huffman minimizes expected symbol-code length among binary prefix codes for the specified symbol probabilities, not among every possible block/arithmetic code.

original.question: Why does increasing M in QAM increase BER?

proposals.reason: Giữ công suất trung bình mà tăng M làm các điểm QAM sít nhau, nhiễu dễ gây nhầm hơn.
proposals.note: At fixed average symbol energy and noise, smaller minimum Euclidean separation generally raises symbol/bit error probability.

original.question: If minimum distance increases, error correction ability will:

options: Not decrease; guaranteed correction is t = floor((d_min − 1)/2), so some increases leave t unchanged

proposals.reason: Số lỗi bảo đảm sửa được t=⌊(dmin−1)/2⌋. Tăng dmin từ 3 lên 4 vẫn chỉ sửa được 1 lỗi, nên không luôn tăng nghiêm ngặt.

original.question: If bandwidth is reduced below Nyquist limit, what occurs?

proposals.note: At fixed Rs, ideal zero-ISI baseband signaling needs bandwidth at least Rs/2; reducing it below this bound prevents zero-ISI pulse shaping.

original.question: Why must baseband signals be modulated onto a carrier?

proposals.reason: Sóng mang đưa thông điệp vào dải RF phù hợp anten và phân kênh; không phải mọi đường truyền baseband đều bắt buộc điều chế lên RF.
proposals.tip: Passband radio → practical antenna + allocated RF band.
proposals.note: Passband radio uses carrier translation for practical antenna radiation and allocation to an RF band; not all wired/baseband links require it.
